target_customer: Finance and operations teams at payments companies, banks and fintechs that need to reconcile large transaction volumes
problem: Finance teams reconcile payments with spreadsheets and rigid legacy tools. Simetrik provides a no-code platform to automate reconciliation and financial controls.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced on volume and modules

founders.name: Alejandro Casas
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (March 2022) says Simetrik was founded in 2019 after a pivot from Ropeo, an ecommerce company from YC Winter 2018, and that his work with payments companies shaped the focus.

founders.name: Santiago Gomez
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder, CFO and COO; TechCrunch calls him COO.

investors: Goldman Sachs Asset Management Growth Equity

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching millions of records across systems with configurable rules is data engineering heavy but built from standard components; the company now claims AI features and 3.5 billion records processed daily.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration with payment flows creates switching costs, but reconciliation software from established vendors exists.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found shows an incumbent copying or acquiring it; it raised a Goldman Sachs-led Series B in 2024.

market_need_then: Rappi, PayU and Mercado Libre were early Latin American customers per a search summary, indicating payment volume growth driving reconciliation pain. The company's own history says a 2019 project with Rappi was pivotal.

brand_strength.rationale: A coined name that evokes symmetry and reconciliation, but no sourced evidence of brand pull; search results mix it up with similarly named firms.

pivots.why: Founders pivoted after the batch; TechCrunch gives the pivot but not the reason, and the company history cites a pivotal Rappi project in 2019

outcome_analysis: Simetrik is the product of a post-YC pivot from the ecommerce startup Ropeo into reconciliation software in 2019. It raised a $20M Series A in 2022, a $55M Series B in 2024 led by Goldman Sachs and a $30M extension in 2025, and claims 180+ clients in 60+ countries. Success stems from a sharper enterprise B2B niche found after the pivot, with large fintech customers in Latin America.
notes: The pivot means the YC W18 company was Ropeo; competitors at the batch were for ecommerce and are not researched, and the reconciliation competitors were not found in a source dated near the 2018 batch, so the list is empty. Series A is $20M per TechCrunch plus $4M venture debt; fintech.global says $24M, which equals the sum. TechCrunch says valuation north of $100M, not given as a figure so post-money is null. The seed led by Cometa has no stated amount or date. The Series B 2024 amount of $55M and the 2025 $30M extension are from search summaries of Yahoo Finance and Mexico Business News; those pages were not opened. CB Insights lists a valuation of $160M to $215M in February 2024 (search snippet only). Total raised about $116M per Yespress and $115.85M per CB Insights. Founder prior employers and education were not found.
